digest.lead: Anthropic secured a massive $5B investment from Amazon with a commitment to spend $100B on AWS cloud services, signaling major enterprise expansion plans.
digest.summary: Meanwhile, Claude Code received incremental updates with improved session management, though speculation continues about potential Pro plan changes.

stories.headline: Anthropic Secures $5B Amazon Investment with $100B Cloud Spending Commitment
stories.summary: Anthropic has received a $5 billion investment from Amazon, committing to spend $100 billion on AWS cloud services in return [1]. The deal has generated significant discussion in the tech community, with over 270 points and 281 comments on Hacker News.
key_points: Investment represents one of the largest AI funding rounds to date
Cloud spending commitment ties Anthropic closely to AWS infrastructure
Deal structure suggests long-term enterprise expansion strategy
stories.impact: This massive funding round positions Anthropic for significant scaling and enterprise market expansion, while the AWS commitment may influence future infrastructure decisions for Claude deployments.

sources.title: Anthropic takes $5B from Amazon and pledges $100B in cloud spending in return

stories.headline: Claude Code v2.1.117 Enhances Session Management and Agent Configuration
stories.summary: The latest Claude Code update introduces forked subagents for external builds via environment variable configuration [1]. The release also improves model selection persistence across restarts and adds session summarization for stale, large sessions in the `/resume` command.
key_points: Forked subagents now available on external builds with CLAUDE_CODE_FORK_SUBAGENT=1
Model selections persist across restarts regardless of project-pinned models
Resume command now offers to summarize large stale sessions before re-reading
stories.impact: These improvements enhance developer productivity by maintaining session context and model preferences, particularly benefiting teams working with long-running development sessions.

stories.headline: Claude Code v2.1.114 Fixes Agent Teams Permission Dialog Crash
stories.summary: A targeted bug fix addresses a crash in the permission dialog that occurred when agent team teammates requested tool permissions [1]. This minor update focuses on stability improvements for collaborative development workflows.
stories.impact: The fix ensures smoother collaboration for development teams using Claude Code's agent teams feature, preventing workflow interruptions during permission requests.

stories.headline: Speculation Grows Around Potential Claude Code Removal from Pro Plans
stories.summary: A social media post has sparked widespread community discussion about potential changes to Claude Code availability in Anthropic's Pro plan [1]. The speculation has generated significant engagement with over 500 comments on Hacker News, though no official confirmation has been provided.
stories.impact: If true, this change could significantly affect individual developers and small teams currently relying on Pro plan access to Claude Code, potentially forcing them to consider enterprise plans or alternative tools.

sources.title: Claude Code to be removed from Anthropic's Pro plan?

stories.headline: Enable forked subagents in external Claude Code builds
stories.summary: Forked subagents allow Claude Code to spawn separate agent processes for parallel task execution. This can improve performance for complex workflows that benefit from concurrent processing.
actionable_steps: Restart Claude Code to apply the setting
Verify subagents are working by checking for multiple agent processes during complex tasks

stories.headline: Use the path parameter with EnterWorktree to switch between git worktrees
stories.summary: The EnterWorktree tool now accepts a path parameter that lets you switch into existing worktrees of your current repository. This makes it easier to work with multiple branches or feature development in parallel without switching repositories.
actionable_steps: Identify the worktree path you want to switch to in your current repository
Use the EnterWorktree tool with the path parameter: `EnterWorktree(path="/path/to/your/worktree")`
Verify you're in the correct worktree by checking the current branch or directory

stories.headline: Use environment variables to configure MCP server settings in Claude Code
stories.summary: Claude Code v2.1.85 introduced CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_NAME and CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_URL environment variables for MCP headersHelper scripts. This allows a single helper script to serve multiple MCP servers, simplifying configuration management.
actionable_steps: Set the CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_NAME environment variable to your desired server name
Set the CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_URL environment variable to your MCP server URL
Update your MCP headersHelper scripts to use these variables instead of hardcoded values

stories.headline: Use `/team-onboarding` command to generate teammate ramp-up guides
stories.summary: Claude Code can automatically create onboarding documentation for new team members based on your local usage patterns. This saves time creating training materials and ensures consistency in how team members learn your workflows.
actionable_steps: Update to Claude Code v2.1.101 or later
Run the `/team-onboarding` command in your Claude Code interface
Review the generated ramp-up guide and customize as needed
Share the guide with new team members

stories.headline: Use `/terminal-setup` to configure smoother fullscreen scrolling in VS Code, Cursor, and Windsurf
stories.summary: Claude Code v2.1.116 improved terminal scrolling performance by automatically configuring your editor's scroll sensitivity. This eliminates choppy scrolling when working in fullscreen terminal mode.
actionable_steps: Open Claude Code in your VS Code, Cursor, or Windsurf editor
Allow Claude Code to configure your editor's scroll sensitivity settings
